tiers.official-primary: Statute, ordinance, regulation, or government agency page. Primary authority.
tiers.official-guidance: Government agency guidance/explainer page. Authoritative interpretation, not the statute text.
tiers.official-org: Official website of the organization named (e.g. the legal-aid provider itself). Not a government source.
tiers.secondary: Commercial or practitioner source. Used only for context and always flagged. Never used as the basis for a value.

sources.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. States 1.6% effective 3/1/26-2/28/27; 30-day notice, 90-day if >10%; +5 days if mailed; notice must state dollar amount, percentage and effective date; no rounding up; base rent only; additional-occupant charge prohibited.

sources.title: Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27 Announced (news, January 14, 2026)
571 Allowable Annual Increases (2026-27 table of every AGA since 1982)
sources.verified: PDF fetched 2026-11-06 and the full year-by-year table read. This is the source for every historical percentage used in the calculations.

sources.title: Banked rent increases
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. States a skipped increase is banked only if at least 24 full months pass without any rent increase; banking allowed since 4/1/1982; no limit; no compounding; notice must identify the banked portion.

sources.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Method: add the percentage for each year together (not compound); no petition needed; no rounding up.

sources.title: Increasing rents during irregular periods
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Covers increases 12-24 months and 24+ months from the anniversary date, and the trade-off of losing an annual increase when the date shifts.

sources.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws (June 13, 1979 coverage date)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Units built on or before June 13, 1979 that are not single-family dwellings generally have rent control and eviction protection.

sources.publisher: San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Rent Ordinance)
sources.title: Sec. 37.3 - Rent Limitations
sources.verified: Ordinance text fetched 2026-11-06. Contains the annual-increase formula (60% of published CPI, cap 7%), banking, notice content requirements per (b)(1)-(5), additional-occupants prohibition at (a)(11), and the null-and-void rule at (b)(5).

sources.publisher: San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Rent Ordinance)
sources.title: Sec. 37.15 - Reporting Obligations; Licensing
sources.verified: Ordinance text fetched 2026-11-06. A rent increase license is required; if the owner has not substantially complied, the license is suspended and the tenant need not pay the increase for the suspension period.

sources.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Annual deadline March 1; a rent increase notice is not enforceable without a license on the effective date of the notice; reporting began March 1, 2023 for buildings with fewer than 10 units.

sources.publisher: San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Rent Ordinance)
sources.title: Sec. 37.10B - Tenant Harassment
sources.verified: Ordinance text fetched 2026-11-06. Includes (a)(5) on rent increases used to influence a tenant to vacate, with the three bad-faith factors, and (a)(9) on discrimination.

sources.title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Lists the six petition-based increases plus the passthroughs that use Rent Board worksheets; a petition must be filed before the notice is served.

sources.title: Operating and Maintenance Expense Petitions (Topic 322)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Up to 7% additional base rent; requires expenses to rise faster than the annual increase; petition must be filed before the notice; tenant hardship application available.

sources.title: Special Circumstances Petitions Based on Rents for Comparable Units (Topic 323)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Directly states that a long-standing tenant paying below market is NOT itself an extraordinary circumstance.

sources.title: Algorithmic devices that set rent are prohibited in San Francisco (Topic 268)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Admin Code Sec. 37.10C effective October 14, 2024; bans sale and use of revenue-management software that uses non-public competitor data to set rent or occupancy.

sources.title: Charging for Additional Occupants Prohibited (Topics 152, 254)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Charging more solely because an occupant was added is an unlawful rent increase even if the lease allows it.

sources.title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins (Topic 153)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. A co-tenant is not subject to an unlimited increase regardless of when the co-tenant moved in; only a subtenant may be, and only with a timely 6.14 notice.

sources.publisher: San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 37 (Rent Ordinance)
sources.title: Sec. 37.9F - Circumvention of Tenant Protections
sources.verified: Ordinance text fetched 2026-11-06.

sources.title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Independently confirms 1.6% / 1.4% / 1.7% for the three most recent periods.

sources.title: Report an unlawful rent increase or request a review of your rent history (Topic 354)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Free tenant petition, no time limit; the hearing process does not require an attorney.

sources.title: Tenant Petitions (Topic 351)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Free to file; the Rent Board does not adjudicate harassment, discrimination or retaliation.

sources.title: Rent Board Forms Center
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Source of the official forms (516A-518) referenced on the tenant-review page.

sources.publisher: SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development (sf.gov)
sources.title: Tenant and Landlord Resources
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Lists the City's designated free tenant counseling organizations and the Bar Association's landlord/tenant mediation service.

sources.title: Civil Code Sec. 827 (rent increase notice periods)
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06. 30 days if 10% or less; 90 days if more than 10%; mail service per Code Civ. Proc. Sec. 1013; subdivision (c) requires the longer of state/local notice periods.

sources.title: Civil Code Sec. 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act / AB 1482 rent cap)
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06. Cap is 5% plus CPI or 10%, whichever is lower; subdivision (d)(3) exempts housing under a local ordinance that restricts increases to less than the state cap.

sources.title: Civil Code Sec. 1946.2 (just cause for termination)
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06.

sources.title: Civil Code Sec. 1942.5 (retaliation)
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06. A rent increase within 180 days of a tenantability complaint is prohibited; (d) bars increases intended to retaliate for tenant organizing.

sources.title: Government Code Sec. 12955 (FEHA housing discrimination)
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06. Lists the protected characteristics including source of income, familial status, disability, marital status, and bars harassment.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
sources.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Federal protected classes: race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability.

sources.publisher: Cornell Legal Information Institute (text of 42 U.S.C.)
sources.title: 42 U.S.C. Sec. 3604 - Discrimination in the sale or rental of housing
sources.verified: Statute text fetched 2026-11-06. (b) bars discrimination in the terms, conditions or privileges of rental because of a protected characteristic. No federal rent ceiling appears in the section.

sources.title: Consumer Price Index, San Francisco Area - August 2026
sources.verified: Release fetched 2026-11-06. CPI-U all items +3.4% over 12 months to August 2026; notes October 2025 data missing due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations - which is the documented reason the 2026-27 AGA used an estimated figure.

sources.title: Property Information Map (building age / permit lookup)
sources.verified: Tool page fetched 2026-11-06. This is the Rent Board's recommended way to confirm a building's year built (S07).

sources.title: Legal Assistance for Tenants
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. EDC describes itself as lead organization of the City's Tenant Right to Counsel program and provides free representation; legal line (415) 659-9184.

sources.title: Resolving Problems With Your Landlord or Tenant (Topic 262, ADR program)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Free Alternative Dispute Resolution program covers housing-related disputes including rent increases.

sources.title: 24 CFR 100.70 - Other prohibited sale and rental conduct
sources.verified: Regulation fetched 2026-11-06. Covers discriminatory terms, conditions and privileges in rental.

sources.title: The Rent Ordinance (index of all Chapter 37 sections)
sources.verified: Page fetched 2026-11-06. Notes the Rent Board's copy is for convenience and that American Legal is the official publisher; last amended 11/2/26.
